newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec finance minister contests auditor's report.
newsitem.headline: Quebec finance minister contests auditor's report.

text.p: The Quebec Finance Ministry said on Thursday it disagreed with the Quebec auditor general's projection that the 1997-1998 provincial deficit would reach C$3.4 billion, C$1.2 billion higher than the ministry forecast.
Finance spokeswoman Andree Corriveau told Reuters the disagreement on the figures was related to the management of the government employees' pension fund.
"We agreed with the auditor in 1979 that we should spread over 50 years the reimbursement of the deficit of the government employees's pension fund. That is our way to calculate the figures."
The Finance Ministry does not include the pension fund figures in the calculation of the debt and the deficit.

Quebec Auditor General Guy Breton said earlier today the provincial government was not giving the right picture on its deficit and debt figures because its financial statements were not consolidated. Consolidated statements include government funds, pension liabilities and financial results for government agencies.
